pharm: Long-acting benzodiazepine; GABA-A receptor positive allosteric modulator
quick: Seizures: start ≤1.5 mg/day in 3 divided doses; max 20 mg/day. Panic: 0.25 mg BID, target 1 mg/day
With or without food; take with water
Risk; AED registry, avoid unless essential
Caution; no specific adjustment but accumulation possible
Caution; contraindicated in significant liver disease
Sedation, dependence, mood/suicidality, periodic taper need
summary: Clonazepam is a long-acting benzodiazepine used for seizure disorders and panic disorder. It carries a boxed warning for the risks of co-use with opioids, and for abuse, dependence, and withdrawal. Stopping abruptly can precipitate seizures and severe withdrawal.
indications: Seizure disorders: Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, akinetic and myoclonic seizures
Absence seizures (petit mal) unresponsive to succinimides
Panic disorder, with or without agoraphobia

dosage.d: Start ≤1.5 mg/day in 3 divided doses; increase by 0.5–1 mg every 3 days as tolerated
Start 0.25 mg BID; increase to target 1 mg/day after 3 days
dosage.n: Some patients up to 4 mg/day; taper by 0.125 mg BID every 3 days to discontinue

dosage.d: Start 0.01–0.03 mg/kg/day (max 0.05 mg/kg/day) in 2–3 doses; maintenance 0.1–0.2 mg/kg/day
Initiate at low end of range, titrate slowly

admin: Swallow tablet whole with water; orally disintegrating tablet placed on tongue to dissolve
Confirm controlled-substance documentation and indication before dispensing
Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration
Titrate gradually; do not stop abruptly
Screen for opioid co-use and substance use history
Provide written guidance on dependence and tapering
moa: Enhances the inhibitory effect of GABA by binding the benzodiazepine site on the GABA-A receptor-chloride channel complex, increasing the frequency of chloride channel opening; this potentiates neuronal inhibition, suppressing seizure spread and producing anxiolytic and sedative effects.

monitor: Respiratory depression if combined CNS depressants

preg: May cause fetal harm; AEDs associated with congenital anomalies. Use only if potential benefit justifies risk. Enroll in the North American Antiepileptic Drug Pregnancy Registry. Neonatal sedation, hypotonia, withdrawal and feeding difficulties reported with late-pregnancy use.
lact: Excreted in human milk. Breastfeeding not recommended; monitor breastfed infant for sedation, lethargy, poor feeding, and apnea if used.
renal: No specific dosing adjustment established; use caution as metabolites may accumulate. Titrate slowly and monitor for excess sedation.
hepatic: Metabolized by the liver; contraindicated in significant hepatic disease. Use caution and reduce dose in mild-moderate impairment.

major: Opioids (boxed warning): profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, death
Strong CYP3A4 inducers (carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital) reduce clonazepam levels
moderate: CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase clonazepam exposure
minor: Caffeine may partially antagonize sedative effect
interactions.food: May be taken without regard to meals; avoid grapefruit in large amounts (minor CYP3A4 effect)
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; additive CNS and respiratory depression, increased impairment and overdose risk
interactions.diagnostics: May affect EEG patterns; no major laboratory test interference established

monitoring: Signs of misuse, abuse, and dependence
Mood changes and suicidality (especially early therapy)
Respiratory status if combined with opioids/CNS depressants
Periodic reassessment of continued need and taper plan
counsel: Do not stop suddenly; tapering required to avoid seizures and withdrawal
Avoid alcohol and other sedatives; tell all prescribers you take this
May impair driving and operating machinery
Habit-forming: take only as prescribed, do not increase dose
Report mood changes, thoughts of self-harm, or unusual behavior
Inform clinician of pregnancy or breastfeeding plans
pearls: Long half-life allows once or twice daily dosing and smoother withdrawal than short-acting benzodiazepines
Tolerance to anticonvulsant effect may develop within months
Flumazenil reverses benzodiazepine overdose but may precipitate seizures in dependent patients
Co-prescription with opioids should be avoided; if unavoidable, use lowest doses and monitor closely
Useful for myoclonic and absence seizures and as adjunct in refractory epilepsy
missed: Take as soon as remembered unless it is near the next dose; do not double up. For scheduled antiepileptic use, maintain regular timing to avoid breakthrough seizures.
overdose: Presents with somnolence, confusion, ataxia, diminished reflexes, hypotension, respiratory depression, and coma, worsened by other CNS depressants. Provide supportive care, airway/ventilation support, and IV fluids; gastric decontamination if early. Flumazenil may be used cautiously but can precipitate seizures and withdrawal in chronic users.
